questions.question: If you are pulled over on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use your taillights to alert other drivers.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Keep your lights off so you don't distract other drivers.
Place items on the road to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers. Also place warning signals to alert other drivers.

questions.question: Parts of an exhaust system should be:

options.text: Loose.
Leaking.
Fastened securely.
Cracked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fastened securely.
questions.explanation: All exhaust system parts must be secure, not loose, broken, or missing. Parts should be properly mounted and should not rub against any moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: ABS allows you to:

options.text: Drive faster.
Brake harder.
Stay in control when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in control when stopping.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps prevent your wheels from locking when you brake hard. You should drive and brake the same way whether your vehicle has ABS or not.

questions.question: When passengers have carry-on baggage, it is best to:

options.text: Place the items in front of the rear exit door.
Leave the items near the front door.
Secure the items so all exits remain easy to reach.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the items so all exits remain easy to reach.
questions.explanation: Baggage must not be left in doorways or aisles. Secure baggage so it will not move, the driver can move freely, passengers can exit through any door or window in an emergency, and riders are safe from falling items.

questions.question: When using your mirrors, you should frequently look at your tires to:

options.text: Watch for tire fires.
See if the tires are rolling properly.
Check if the tread is in good condition.
Compare the tire size to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for tire fires.
questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to spot a tire fire if one starts. Tire fires happen when tires are under-inflated, when dual tires touch each other, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: Skids happen when:

options.text: Tires lose their grip on the road.
There is too much weight in the trailer.
ABS activates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose their grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Skids occur when tires lose traction with the road. This can happen from braking too hard, accelerating too fast, steering too sharply, or driving too fast.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no higher than three feet.
Should be secured to prevent it from moving during transport.
Should have the heaviest items placed on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent it from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured so it will not move while the vehicle is in use. Loose cargo is dangerous to you and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: Most hazardous materials:

options.text: Should be stored near the engine of a bus.
May be transported on a bus if passengers are told in advance.
Can be transported on a bus if stored near the rear of the vehicle.
Cannot be transported by bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be transported by bus.
questions.explanation: With a few exceptions, hazardous materials are not allowed on buses. Your passengers' safety is your responsibility.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because you may not see everything behind your vehicle. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be parked on an uphill slope.
Should be parked on a downhill slope.
Must be washed.
May need to have the engine running.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to have the engine running.
questions.explanation: For some vehicles, the engine must be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always stop completely.
May need to turn your vehicle sharply to get out of the way.
Should change lanes without looking.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to turn your vehicle sharply to get out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you don't have enough space to stop safely, turning sharply to get out of the way may be your best option.

questions.question: The steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with both hands.
Held with one hand so you can eat or drink.
Held with one hand at a time, switching between hands.
Cracked to improve your grip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Held with both hands.
questions.explanation: To control your vehicle properly, hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Turn the steering wheel as hard as possible.
Not use the brakes.
Put the vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, do not use the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down. This will help you regain traction.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, use your brakes mainly by:

options.text: Using engine power to slow down and downshifting.
Using the brake pedal.
Using the parking brake.
Using ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using engine power to slow down and downshifting.
questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use your engine to control your speed. Downshift before you start going down the hill to help you slow down safely.

questions.question: A bus should be refueled:

options.text: Inside a building while passengers are on board.
Anywhere while passengers are on board.
Without passengers on board, except when absolutely necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Without passengers on board, except when absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless it is absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.
Freeze before other road surfaces.
Have heaters built in to prevent freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful when crossing bridges if the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: After a trailer starts to turn while backing, you should follow the trailer by:

options.text: Doing nothing. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
Turning the steering wheel farther in the same direction.
Using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When backing a vehicle with a trailer, turn the steering wheel the opposite way from where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: The standee line:

options.text: Is a line on the floor that passengers cannot cross.
Is a single line of standing passengers.
Shows the maximum number of people allowed on the bus.
Shows how tall passengers may be.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a line on the floor that passengers cannot cross.
questions.explanation: While a bus is moving, passengers may not stand ahead of the rear of the driver's seat. Buses that allow standing passengers must have a two-inch line on the floor to show where passengers cannot stand. This is called the standee line.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of distraction?

options.text: Physical
Mental
Obtuse

questions.correctAnswerText: Obtuse
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving fall into two types: physical (like reaching for something) and mental (like talking to a passenger). Some things, like using a hand-held phone, are both types.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard for the driver to see behind the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the vehicle.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
Trailers are not designed to drive in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard for the driver to see behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only drive in reverse if it is absolutely necessary.
